sentences.text:
Durga vs Shabbir @ Shabir on 8 October, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:29401
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 8 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2356 of 2024
 Durga And Others
 Versus
 Shabbir @ Shabir And Others
 Appearance:

Shri Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellants.
 Shri Sudarshan Pandit, Advocate with Shri Rajesh Pand  counsel for respondent No.2.
 ORDER

The present Misc. Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 12.12.2023 passed by the I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, Dist. Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No.268/2022 challenging the quantum of compensation.

entities.text: I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, Dist. Dhar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 01.08.2022 at around 04:00 PM, Gudda along with his wife deceased maylibai was travelling by motorcycle bearing registration number MP-11-MZ-6890 to their village Ganga Talai.
At that time, an Eicher vehicle bearing registration number MH-04-EY-5477 being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner, came and dashed into the motorcycle of the Gudda.
As a result, Gudda and his wife fell down.

After hitting them, the said vehicle attempted NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29401 2 MA-2356-2024 to flee from the spot and in doing so, collided with another motorcycle on which Dinesh and Dharmendra were riding.
Due to the impact, Dinesh suffered grievous injuries and was rushed to a hospital in Dhar, where he was declared dead.
2.1 The claimants / appellants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Dinesh.

The Claims Tribunal, after considering the evidence available on record, awarded a total compensation of Rs.16,01,400/- out of which Rs.14,36,400/-
was awarded towards loss of dependency.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal has incorrectly assessed the income of the deceased.
At the time of accident, he was earning Rs.40,000/- per month as a mason.

However, the Claims Tribunal disbelieved this claim and erroneously considered his income at Durga vs Shabbir @ Shabir on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20411326/
1 Rs.7,600/- per month on a notional basis by treating him as an unskilled labourer.

3.1 Learned counsel further submits that while awarding compensation under the head of loss of consortium, the Claims Tribunal has granted only Rs.44,000/- each to three claimants i.e. the widow and two children.

However, no compensation under this head has been awarded to the mother and father of the deceased, who are also entitled to the same in light of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782 .

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He, therefore, prays for enhancement of the compensation awarded.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supports the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29401 3 MA-2356-2024 findings of the award and submits that there was no material evidence whatsoever regarding the income of the deceased.

He refers to the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in para 34 of the impugned award and submits that apart from the statement of Durgabai (AW-2), the wife of the deceased, no other evidence was produced.
Thus, the Claims Tribunal has rightly discarded the claim regarding the deceased's income.

He, therefore,
prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

From perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it is observed that apart from the statement of Durgabai (AW-2), there is no material evidence to establish that the deceased was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Hence, the Claims Tribunal in the considered view of this Court has rightly disbelieved such claim.
However, the income of the deceased was fixed on a notional basis at Rs.7,600/- per month.
In view of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, this appears to be incorrect.
At the time of the accident, the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer were Rs.9,125/-, which should be taken as the income of the deceased.
7. As regards compensation for consortium, it has already been held by the Honb'le Apex Court in the case of Magma (Supra) that the mother and father are also entitled to filial consortium.
Accordingly, both are hereby awarded Rs.44,000/- each.
8. In view of the above modifications and additions, the compensation for loss of dependency now amounts to Rs.17,24,625/- and the total compensation comes to Rs.19,77,625/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29401 4 MA-2356-2024 9.
After deducting the amount already awarded of Rs.16,01,400/-, the appellants are entitled to receive Rs.3,76,225/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10. This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
11. It is seen from the record that the appeal has been valued at Rs.3,00,000/-.
The appellants are required to pay the deficit Court fee within four weeks from today.

If the court fee is not paid within Durga vs Shabbir @ Shabir on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20411326/
2 four weeks, then interest will not apply on the enhanced amount beyond the period of four weeks.
12. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
